tabs.title: Company Overview
tabs.content:
**Palmsera Health** is a healthcare provider that stores patient records and clinical imaging in Azure. The company must meet strict regulatory requirements for data confidentiality and network isolation.

**Current Environment:**
- A hub VNet centralizes shared security services; more than a dozen clinical-application spoke VNets are peered to the hub.
- Clinical application tiers (web, API, database) run in separate subnets within each spoke, with traffic between tiers tightly restricted.
- All outbound internet access from spokes must be inspected and filtered centrally rather than allowed directly from each spoke.

tabs.title: Compliance & Security Requirements
tabs.content:
**Segmentation:**
- Within a spoke VNet, the API tier subnet must be able to reach the database tier subnet on port 1433 only; all other inbound traffic to the database subnet must be denied, including traffic from the same virtual network that isn't explicitly permitted.
- The security team has created a custom NSG rule at priority 100 that denies all inbound traffic to the database subnet, and a second rule at priority 200 that allows port 1433 from the API subnet.

**Centralized filtering:**
- All spokes must send outbound internet-bound traffic through a single, centrally managed, stateful firewall in the hub VNet that supports FQDN-based application rules and can apply consistent policy across every spoke via one management plane.

**Private data access:**
- The Azure SQL Managed Instance and Storage account used for clinical records must be reachable from every spoke over a private IP address, and name resolution for these services must work correctly for spokes that don't have their own custom DNS server — a single private DNS zone strategy linked to all relevant VNets is required.
